summary: Representative Feenstra has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. The one statement found, a candidate questionnaire answer, calls for "commonsense, enforceable guardrails" that protect privacy and jobs in Iowa while supporting economic growth and innovation.

Representative Fulcher has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their statements on AI are about keeping American leadership in AI, the competition with China, European AI rules, limits on state AI laws and energy for AI.
Representative Simpson has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. The only AI posts found promote AI infrastructure and winning the AI race, without discussing risks from the technology.

Representative Jackson has acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI by co-signing a letter, but not in their own words. A letter they co-signed warns that AI is "hurtling toward a future that, minus guardrails, could endanger humanity." Their own posts on AI are about government reliance on AI and an AI-generated map error.

Representative Kelly has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their statements on AI are about health insurers using AI to deny claims, saying "physicians and science-backed medicine" must guide decisions, and about children's safety and privacy.

Representative Ramirez has acknowledged serious risks from AI in general terms by co-signing letters, but not in their own words. A letter they co-signed says "Congress must act before such an incident leads to a much larger catastrophe." Their own statements are about AI replacing workers, privacy, civil rights and regulating AI companies.

Representative García has acknowledged that AI could threaten human survival. They have said unchecked AI development "threatens our economy, democracy, and humanity itself" and called for a ban on superintelligence and a pause on advanced AI development.

Representative Quigley has acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI by co-signing a letter, but not in their own words. The letter names risks of "agentic misalignment, mass cybersecurity breaches, and development of biological or chemical weapons." Their own statements are about an AI-generated video, data center energy and a student AI app.

Representative Casten has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their posts on AI are about data center energy costs, AI chip sales and corruption, and the use of AI in government and its effect on federal jobs.

Representative Krishnamoorthi has acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI, without describing it as a threat of extinction. They have said AI can threaten "biological security, and even nuclear command and control," and called for safeguards "that keep humans firmly in control" of self-improving systems.

Representative Schakowsky has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their statements on AI are about holding Big Tech accountable, trade rules that could block AI regulation, consumer protection and children's privacy.

Representative Schneider has acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI by co-signing a letter, but not in their own words. A letter they co-signed warns that AI is "hurtling toward a future that, minus guardrails, could endanger humanity." Their only other AI post found is about data center electricity costs.

Representative Foster has acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI, without describing it as a threat of extinction. They have warned of AI agents that "could evade human oversight" and said software-only controls "will not be sufficient to contain superhuman AI." They have also warned about AI helping people make bioweapons.

Representative Bost has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their posts on AI promote investment in AI and manufacturing, including from Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Nvidia and Apple.

Representative Budzinski has acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI, without describing it as a threat of extinction. They have said "warnings about loss of control from those who have worked in AI, cannot be ignored," and co-signed a letter naming risks such as biological or chemical weapons.

Representative Underwood has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their posts on AI are about guardrails and transparency for data centers, their effect on communities, and the privacy of health data shared with AI chatbots.

Representative LaHood has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their statements on AI are about competition with China, keeping AI chips from adversaries, AI security against foreign threats and data center electricity costs.

Representative Sorensen has acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI by co-signing a letter, but not in their own words. The letter names risks of "agentic misalignment, mass cybersecurity breaches, and development of biological or chemical weapons." Their own posts on AI do not discuss catastrophic risk.

Representative Yakym has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their statements on AI are almost all about data center electricity costs, saying "Hoosiers and their businesses should not be footing the bill for AI data centers."

Representative Stutzman has dismissed warnings of catastrophic risk from AI. Responding to an AI whistleblower, they wrote "The world isn’t ending, AI companies just need to learn responsibility" for their products. Their other AI statements are about American AI leadership and financial regulators' technology.

Representative Baird has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their statements on AI are about oversight of AI chip sales to adversaries, beating China in AI, and science and technology training for diplomats.

Representative Spartz has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their posts on AI are about data centers, including their effect on utility rates, the grid and water, tax credits for them, and AI's effect on jobs.

Representative Shreve has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. The main statement found is an op-ed about foreign scam centers that "weaponize artificial intelligence" to defraud Americans; their other AI posts do not discuss catastrophic risk.

Representative Carson has acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI by co-signing a letter, but not in their own words. The letter names risks including "agentic misalignment" and biological or chemical weapons. In their own words, they have said AI can make cyberattacks and biological weapons "potentially much more dangerous" and pointed to "the risk of rogue AI agents."
Representative Messmer has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. The only AI posts found are about the energy costs of data centers and the use of AI in classrooms.

Representative Houchin has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their statements on AI are about children's safe use of AI chatbots, data center energy costs and a single federal AI framework to avoid "falling behind China".

Representative Schmidt has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. A handful of posts mentioning AI were found, on everyday issues of the kind that come up around AI, and none discusses a catastrophic risk.

Representative Davids has acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI by co-signing a letter, but not in their own words. The letter names risks of "agentic misalignment, mass cybersecurity breaches, and development of biological or chemical weapons." In their own words, they have said "we cannot ignore the real dangers" of AI, naming risks to children and energy costs.

Representative Comer has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their statements on AI are about American AI leadership, government use of AI, opposing heavy AI regulation, and an investigation into a Delaware proposal for AI-run companies.

Representative Guthrie has acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI only as misuse by people, such as bioterrorism, not as a danger from AI systems themselves. They have said that with advances in AI and synthetic biology, "bad actors and foreign adversaries" have greater access to scientific research. Other statements concern the AI race with China and data centers.

Representative McGarvey has acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI by co-signing a letter, but not in their own words. The letter names risks of "agentic misalignment, mass cybersecurity breaches, and development of biological or chemical weapons." Their own AI posts are about local data centers and strain on the power grid.

Representative Massie has dismissed warnings of catastrophic risk from AI. They mocked warnings from AI companies with the post "This week it AI is going to kill us!" Their other AI posts are about data centers, legal immunity for them, and AI-generated attack ads.

Representative Rogers has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. The one statement found is about making data centers pay their own electricity costs, with a strategy that "locks in benefits for Rural America".

Representative Scalise has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their statements on AI are about winning the AI race with China, letting communities decide on data centers, and a national AI framework instead of state laws.
Representative Carter has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their statements on AI are about a cybersecurity task force on AI, data center jobs, utility costs and community impact.

Representative Higgins has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. Their statements on AI are about keeping automated content out of public comments on federal rules, defending a moratorium on state AI laws, and AI-generated videos.

Representative Johnson has dismissed warnings of catastrophic risk from AI. Asked about warnings that superintelligence could end humanity, they said "you're not all going to be dead in 10 years. That's a hoax." They have opposed an emergency moratorium on AI, while saying some oversight and outside auditing would help.
Representative Fields has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. The only AI post found announces new federal funding for equipment that includes an AI supercomputer.

Representative Neal has not acknowledged catastrophic risk from AI. The one statement found supports a limited pilot program using AI at the IRS "with clear guardrails" to detect identity theft and fraud.

Representative McGovern has acknowledged that AI could threaten human survival. They have called on Congress to "confront the existential threat of AI" and, citing experts, said a chance that AI "could wipe out humanity within a decade" is unacceptable even at a fraction.
